explainedBy: Two participants are seated facing each other for a conversation study with a secret assignment.

storyboard.claim: Researchers set up paired conversations with one subject assigned a secret task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two subjects, a man and a woman, seated opposite each other engaged in discussion in a research room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the Boston/Yale research experiment sequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the paired subjects and experimental dialogue setup.

explainedBy: The instruction forces one partner to stare intently to track the other person's blinks.

storyboard.claim: The secret task instructs one subject to count every single blink.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The man looks closely at the woman's eyes while she blinks during the conversation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the secret task instruction to the conversation setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Focuses the visual interaction on observing eye blinks.

explainedBy: The counting task forces an unbroken, intense gaze between the participants.

storyboard.claim: Counting blinks forces relentless, unbroken eye contact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The man locks eyes in an unblinking, direct stare at the woman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Maintains the pair as the stare intensifies into unbroken lock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the physical reality of the counting task: locked stare.

explainedBy: The stared-at participant develops an unexpected feeling of affection and fondness.

storyboard.claim: Stared-at subjects reported significantly higher fondness and respect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The stared-at partner smiles warmly and reaches toward the heart icon appearing beside them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the experimental result of the prolonged eye contact.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates the positive emotional payoff of fondness with a heart.

explainedBy: The host questions whether staring alone works, confirmed to be physiological rather than a trick.

storyboard.claim: The reaction is physiological biology, not merely a psychological illusion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man looking startled and questioning how staring triggers an actual physical reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the experiment's behavioral result to its biological cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes the biological reality behind the psychological effect.

explainedBy: Intense eye contact triggers an immediate chain of adrenaline and phenylethylamine release.

storyboard.claim: Eye contact shoots adrenaline and phenylethylamine through the recipient's veins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A causal chain flowing from eye contact through adrenaline surge to chemical PEA release.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Diagrams the biological mechanism introduced in the prior beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the step-by-step neurochemical cascade.

explainedBy: The chemical PEA released by eye contact is identical to the hormone of early romance and falling in love.

storyboard.claim: PEA is the exact hormone released during erotic excitement or falling in love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The causal diagram continues as the token tag relabels from excitement to falling in love.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the causal diagram to reveal the hormone's romantic nature.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the conversational eye contact hormone to romance biology.

explainedBy: Lowndes introduces the technique Sticky Eyes, stretching gaze contact until it reluctantly breaks.

storyboard.claim: Lowndes names this technique Sticky Eyes: stretching eye contact like warm taffy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla holds an engaged gaze on the man, holding eye contact past the expected moment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the formal technique resulting from the chemical mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the prolonged gaze as an intentional social tool.

explainedBy: The speaker pushes back: an uncalibrated blank stare at co-workers risks disciplinary action.

storyboard.claim: Uncalibrated staring at colleagues triggers fear of workplace HR complaints.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried professional slumped in an office setting realizing the hazard of unblinking staring.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the idealized technique with real-world workplace risks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the risk in common professional anxiety.

explainedBy: The book illustrates uncalibrated staring with the story of Zola terrified by the family cat.

storyboard.claim: Housekeeper Zola was terrified by the family Siamese cat's unbroken gaze.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla recoils with hands raised in fear, demonstrating Zola's terror at an unblinking gaze.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the cautionary tale of the predatory cat stare.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts visceral fear caused by cold, unbroken stares.

explainedBy: The emotionless cat sat on the stairs staring into her soul, signaling predatory intent.

storyboard.claim: An unbroken stare in nature signals predatory calculation, not respect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A seated figure adopting a cold, unblinking predatory posture on the steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the cat's stare terrified the housekeeper.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects cold stillness with primal threat signals.

explainedBy: In nature an unbroken stare means a predator calculating the trajectory to bite your neck.

storyboard.claim: In the wild, unbroken staring is a lethal predatory calculation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sharp, aggressive posture pointing directly forward, embodying predator focus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Delivers the evolutionary explanation of unbroken gaze.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dramatizes the animal threat of calculating an attack.

explainedBy: Prolonged eye contact without warm calibration is interpreted by the brain as an existential threat.

storyboard.claim: Prolonged eye contact is a primal threat signal if it lacks calibration.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man reflecting anxiously on how gaze without warmth triggers instinctual danger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Translates the predator anecdote into human communication theory.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies lack of calibration as the cause of social creepiness.

explainedBy: The assumption that staring creates fondness fails when men stare at men, provoking hostility.

storyboard.claim: Male subjects stared at by another man felt hostility rather than fondness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A refute diagram showing universal staring rejected when tested on male-to-male pairs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Refutes the universal claim of uncalibrated eye contact.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reveals the gender boundary discovered by the Yale study.

refute.truth: CALIBRATED EYE CONTACT BY GENDER DYNAMICS

explainedBy: Prolonged male gaze fires adrenaline into a fight-or-flight response rather than a chemical bonding response.

storyboard.claim: Adrenaline triggers fight-or-flight rather than bonding when gaze is miscalibrated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The refute diagram highlights the reason: threat response replacing the PEA surge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the refute diagram with the physiological reason.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows adrenaline diverted to fight-or-flight instead of bonding.

explainedBy: Micro-calibration is essential: men must adjust eye contact intensity when speaking to men.

storyboard.claim: Micro-calibration requires moderating eye contact when speaking man-to-man.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman explains the necessity of fine-tuning gaze intensity in conversations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Presents micro-calibration as the solution to gaze hostility.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes conscious calibration as the core rule.

explainedBy: In male conversation, especially on vulnerable topics, the gaze must break naturally.

storyboard.claim: Eye contact between men must break naturally during vulnerable topics.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman gestures turning gaze away slightly, demonstrating a comfortable release of tension.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specifies how to execute micro-calibration between men.
storyboard.addedInformation: Illustrates releasing gaze to reduce conversational pressure.

explainedBy: Sticky eye contact is held warmly with women to cultivate genuine empathetic rapport.

storyboard.claim: Sticky eyes can be held longer with women to build empathetic engagement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man and woman in conversation sharing warm, sustained, empathetic eye contact.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts male-to-male calibration with mixed-gender engagement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows warm, attentive focus in social dialogue.

explainedBy: The gaze functions as an empathetic tether anchoring your complete attention to their words.

storyboard.claim: The gaze acts as an empathetic anchor signaling total absorption in the other's words.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener leans in attentively with a supportive hand reach while the partner speaks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clarifies that sticky eyes are an empathetic anchor, not a blank stare.
storyboard.addedInformation: Demonstrates listening through engaged physical posture.

explainedBy: Social calibration operates like dialing down the wattage of attention depending on the partner.

storyboard.claim: Social awareness means dialing attention wattage up or down depending on the audience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum scale showing attention intensity adjusted between low and high wattage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the dynamic calibration rule as an adjustable spectrum.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes attention as a continuum rather than on/off.

explainedBy: Techniques like sticky eyes are not about manipulative sales tricks or hypnotizing clients.

storyboard.claim: Sticky eyes and flooding smiles are not cheap hypnosis or sales manipulation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man sets aside a false smiling mask, rejecting superficial social manipulation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dispels the misconception that these techniques are cynical sales tricks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the mask icon to reject dishonest manipulation.

explainedBy: True calibration choreographs emotional safety, offering a secure harbor for their primitive brain.

storyboard.claim: Mastery is choreographing emotional safety as an exclusive harbor for their primitive brain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla stands confidently holding a protective shield, symbolizing emotional safety.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the true goal: building psychological and biological safety.
storyboard.addedInformation: Represents interpersonal trust with a protective shield.

explainedBy: Facial safety must be grounded by physical body posture to establish complete rapport.

storyboard.claim: Facial rapport must be reinforced and grounded by full physical posture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram linking facial safety directly to bodily physical safety.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bridges facial micro-calibration to whole-body posturing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Maps the transition from facial cues to postural alignment.

explainedBy: The hosts introduce the big baby pivot and epaulet posture as foundational physical tools.

storyboard.claim: The next core techniques are the Big Baby Pivot and the Epaulet Posture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla introduces the postural techniques with an upright, deliberate stance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Announces the two primary physical alignment techniques.
storyboard.addedInformation: Opens the narrative demonstration scene.

explainedBy: Carla steps into a packed corporate mixer surrounded by intimidating industry leaders.

storyboard.claim: A high-stakes corporate mixer crowded with industry heavyweights.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla steps tentatively into an upscale, intimidating corporate networking room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the story scene setting for Carla's case study.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places Carla in the high-pressure social mixer environment.

explainedBy: Carla, recently divorced and re-entering the professional scene, feels vulnerable and anxious.

storyboard.claim: Carla is a recently divorced copywriter trying to re-enter professional networking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla slumps slightly, conveying vulnerability and self-conscious hesitation in the crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals Carla's personal backstory and vulnerability.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows emotional anxiety behind her guarded physical posture.

explainedBy: Carla hides near an architectural pillar, casting nervous half-smiles over her shoulder.

storyboard.claim: Carla hides by a pillar, casting nervous defensive half-smiles over her shoulder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla shelters against a pillar, casting a strained half-smile over her angled shoulder.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Depicts Carla's defensive, closed-off body language.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes the hesitant over-the-shoulder smile mistake.

explainedBy: Because her body is angled defensively away, passing guests quickly lose interest and walk off.

storyboard.claim: When a torso is angled away, people lose interest and wander off.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla's angled, averted posture causes prospective conversationalists to walk away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the negative consequence of an angled body posture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Demonstrates how angled shoulders repel social approaches.

explainedBy: Suddenly Carla feels a gentle tug on her skirt: it is the hostess's five-year-old son Willie.

storyboard.claim: The hostess's five-year-old son Willie gives a tiny tug on Carla's skirt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla stops in surprise as she feels a tug from a child down at her skirt.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The unexpected interruption that breaks Carla's guarded posture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the non-threatening child trigger.

explainedBy: Instantly Carla drops all defense and pivots her entire torso one hundred percent toward the child.

storyboard.claim: Carla drops her defensive shoulder angle and pivots 100 percent toward the child.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla turns her full chest and face directly toward the child, radiating welcoming warmth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sudden transformation in posture upon greeting a child.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts complete physical re-orientation with open arms.

explainedBy: Carla bends down with wide eyes, completely absorbed in greeting young Willie.

storyboard.claim: Her eyes widen with complete warmth as she greets the child by name.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla reaches forward with an open, genuine, beaming smile of undivided affection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the genuine, unguarded interaction with Willie.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows total, uninhibited social warmth in action.

explainedBy: What Carla did instinctively with the child is what Lowndes defines as the Big Baby Pivot.

storyboard.claim: Carla's instinctive pivot toward a child is the definition of the Big Baby Pivot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman explains how Carla's natural reaction embodies the core technique.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extracts the universal technique from Carla's specific story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies the instinctive child greeting as the master template.

explainedBy: In an adult networking room this pivot is potent because adults secretly crave undivided attention.

storyboard.claim: Applying this pivot to adults is potent because everyone craves total acceptance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman speaks with authority about applying full-torso orientation to adult peers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the child reaction to adult professional environments.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why adults respond powerfully to total physical presence.

explainedBy: Orienting your torso and literal heart center toward an interlocutor satisfies primitive security needs.

storyboard.claim: Turning your chest and heart center directly toward someone satisfies deep safety needs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman stands facing Carla chest-to-chest, gesturing toward the heart center between them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the physical geometry of full frontal alignment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects chest orientation to emotional heart center alignment.

explainedBy: An angled torso triggers primitive suspicion of someone preparing to flee or concealing a weapon.

storyboard.claim: An angled torso signals primitive suspicion: fleeing or concealing a weapon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter diagram displaying the primitive brain's two suspicions for angled postures.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Analyzes the subconscious threat interpretation of being angled away.
storyboard.addedInformation: Classifies the evolutionary threat signals of oblique posture.

explainedBy: Opening your chest completely offers an undivided acknowledgement of the other person's status.

storyboard.claim: Opening your chest completely grants undivided acknowledgement of their status.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla and Everyman stand facing each other squarely, engaged in mutual respectful dialogue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the angled threat with total open acknowledgement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows frontal orientation conveying respect and status.

explainedBy: Full frontal attention proves you are not scanning the room for someone more important.

storyboard.claim: Full frontal attention signals: I am not scanning the room for someone more important.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Carla offers focused attention directly to the listener without glancing around.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Eliminates the anxiety of divided attention in conversation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes locked, unhurried, presence-centered focus.

explainedBy: A full pivot requires a physical counterbalance: you must hold your space with strong posture.

storyboard.claim: A full pivot requires physical grounding: holding your space with solid posture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman stands upright and grounded, demonstrating deliberate posturing balance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the structural posture needed to support the pivot.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stresses stability so the pivot does not appear servile.

explainedBy: The book introduces the hang-by-your-teeth epaulet posture, inspired by circus acrobats.

storyboard.claim: The Hang-by-Your-Teeth technique draws inspiration from circus acrobats.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman gestures toward a stage setting, introducing the circus acrobat metaphor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions to the acrobat visualization for upright posture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Evokes high-wire acrobatic poise and spinal extension.

explainedBy: Imagine the great Wendez circus acrobats preparing to race into the center ring with proud carriage.

storyboard.claim: Acrobats prepare to enter the center ring with total spinal poise and confidence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman points forward into the spotlighted arena, holding a proud, lengthened posture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes chunk 2 by framing the acrobatic posture at the arena entrance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the threshold bite-bar visualization of the next chunk.
